title: Semistable locus and the exceptional-tree local criterion
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(C,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve with smooth generic fibre and etale generic marking, and let $q:(Y,E)\to(C,D)$ be an $\eta$-modification [def-trf-multipointed-curve-modification]. Let $x\in C$ have image $s\in T$ and be closed in $C_s$, and put $Z=q^{-1}(x)$ for the scheme-theoretic inverse image. Assume $C$ is normal and $Z$ is a one-dimensional curve contained in the semistable locus of $(Y,E)$. The semistable locus is the open locus where the geometric curve fibres are smooth or have completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, the marking is etale over $T$, and the marking is disjoint from the relative singular locus. Then $(C,D)$ is semistable at $x$ if and only if $Z$ is an exceptional projective-line tree over $\kappa(s)$ in the sense of Appendix B: after the residue-field algebraic closure, $Z$ is a connected reduced nodal curve whose irreducible components are smooth projective lines and whose incidence graph is a tree, and
$$|\partial_{Y_s}(Z)|+|E_s\cap Z|\le 2,$$
where $\partial_{Y_s}(Z)=Z\cap\overline{Y_s\setminus Z}$ in $Y_s$. A tree has one vertex per component and one edge per node; the boundary and marked-point counts are geometric-point counts. No reduced subscheme is substituted for the scheme-theoretic fibre $Z$.

proof.text: The semistable locus is open. The nodal-family fitting lemma makes the relative smooth locus open and identifies its complement with the nonsmooth locus; it also gives the open locus whose geometric fibres have only ordinary nodes. The marking map is flat and locally finitely presented by the multipointed-curve definition, and its etale locus is open because etale is flat, locally finitely presented and unramified, while the unramified-locus lemma makes the unramified locus open. Intersecting these opens and the inverse image of the relative smooth locus gives the semistable locus. The semistable marked-base-change lemma supplies the corresponding geometric-fibre and marking assertions after any residue-field extension.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(i), printed p. 34, with the definition of semistable locus; Stacks Tags 0C59, 0C5B and 0475.

proof.text: Fix an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(s)$. Base change of the semistable source and marking is semistable by the semistable-marked-base-change lemma, including preservation of the relative smooth locus. The nodal geometric-fibres-reduced lemma applies to the finite-type fibre of $Y\to T$ and shows that its geometric base changes are reduced. Since $\kappa(s)$ is separably closed for a finite-height valuation ring with separably closed fraction field, the geometric-components lemma identifies irreducible components before and after extension to $\Omega$. Consequently the scheme-theoretic fibre $Z$ base-changes to the fibre used in the exceptional-tree count; nodes, incidence, and the boundary intersection are obtained by the same base change. This is a comparison of $Z$ with $Z_\Omega$, not a replacement of $Z$ by $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.2, printed pp. 30--31, and standing finite-height valuation hypotheses in §4.

proof.text: The criterion is local at $x$. Localize $V$ at $s$ and shrink the normal curve $C$ so that it is connected affine and $x$ is the only closed point of the modification locus. The valuation-curve projective-preparation lemma embeds this normal affine curve into a normal projective $T$-curve with geometrically reduced fibres and extends the modification by the identity away from the chosen neighbourhood. The same lemma allows the relative normalization of the semistable source; the geometrically-reduced-eta-normal lemma says this finite eta-modification is an isomorphism on the semistable source, so the neighbourhood of $Z$ and its scheme-theoretic fibre are unchanged. We therefore obtain a proper projective modification $\bar q:\bar Y\to\bar C$ with geometrically reduced fibres, still semistable near $Z$, and with the same local fibre. No smoothness of $C\to T$ is inferred from normality; a nodal special fibre of a normal total space is allowed.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.2 proof, printed pp. 30--31, local-to-projective reduction; Lemma 4.4.1(i),(ii), printed p. 30.

proof.text: After the preceding replacement, $\bar Y$ and $\bar C$ are proper flat finitely presented curves over the localized valuation base, their fibres are geometrically reduced, and the generic fibres are identified. Apply proper-flat perfect base change to the structure sheaves. The resulting perfect complexes are represented locally by bounded finite-projective complexes; over the local valuation base their terms are free. Tensoring with the generic field and with $\Omega$ preserves the alternating sum of the ranks, so $\chi(\bar Y_\Omega)=\chi(\bar Y_\eta)$ and $\chi(\bar C_\Omega)=\chi(\bar C_\eta)$. Hence the two proper geometric curves in the local reduction have equal arithmetic genus. The connectedness of the relevant projective component is the normal-target connectedness conclusion used in Temkin's reduction.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.2 proof, printed p. 30, connectedness and constant Euler-Poincare characteristic; Appendix B, Corollary B.2.

proof.text: Apply the proper marked curve contraction criterion supplied by Appendix B Corollary B.2 to $\bar q_\Omega$ and the fibre $Z_\Omega$. Equal arithmetic genus and the isomorphism off the contracted point give: the target curve point is an ordinary $n$-fold point exactly when $Z_\Omega$ is a projective-line tree, with $n=|\partial(Z_\Omega)|$. The marking part is the same local calculation: the marking is etale off the modification point by Step 1, and every marked point lying over the contracted point is counted in $E_s\cap Z$; if $n=2$ the bound forces no marking at the node, while if $n=1$ a single marked point is allowed at the smooth point. Thus the pair is semistable at $x$ exactly when $Z$ is an exceptional projective-line tree and $|\partial_{Y_s}(Z)|+|E_s\cap Z|\le2$. This gives both implications and does not appeal to a criterion whose target is assumed smooth.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.2, printed pp. 30--31, and Appendix B Corollary B.2, printed pp. 56--57.

proof.text: Finally, the projective replacement is unchanged on the neighbourhood containing $Z$, and all constructions commute with the algebraic-closure base change in Step 2. Therefore the tree, node, boundary, and marking counts just obtained are exactly the counts for the original scheme-theoretic fibre $Z=q^{-1}(x)$. The statement uses no assertion that nilpotents or embedded points may be discarded; the source's geometrically reduced replacement proves that the fibre appearing in the criterion is the same fibre, not merely the same underlying support.
